entries_new.name: Free Republic of Rehoboth
entries_new.founder: Baster community (left the Cape Colony in 1868)
entries_new.laws: Constitution known as the Vaderlike Wette (Paternal Laws)
entries_new.challenge: German colonial rule, later South Africa and then Namibia
entries_new.mechanism: Self-government of a settler community under its own constitution and elected Kaptein, on land outside the Cape Colony.
entries_new.story: The Basters are a community in central Namibia descended from Nama people and Europeans. They left the British-ruled Cape Colony in 1868 and settled on a plateau between the Namib and Kalahari deserts. In 1872 they set up the Free Republic of Rehoboth around the town of Rehoboth, under a written constitution called the Vaderlike Wette (Paternal Laws). Wikipedia states that after Namibian independence in 1990 the new state took their territory without compensation, and that a town council replaced the Chief's Council. The Baster leader, the Kaptein, has no official status under the constitution of Namibia.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states
Wikipedia: Basters

entries_new.name: Griqualand West
entries_new.stopped_by: Annexation by the Cape Colony in 1880
entries_new.story: Griqualand West is a region of about 40,000 square kilometres in what is now South Africa's Northern Cape. The Griqua, a semi-nomadic, Afrikaans-speaking people of mixed Khoikhoi and Dutch descent, set up several states beyond the Cape Colony's frontier. Wikipedia dates de facto independence here from the founding of Griquatown in 1813. In 1873 the territory was proclaimed a British colony with Kimberley as capital, a status that neither Britain nor the neighbouring Cape Colony recognised, according to the list entry. The Cape Colony annexed it in 1880.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states
Wikipedia: Griqualand West

entries_new.name: Griqualand East
entries_new.stopped_by: British occupation (1874) and incorporation into the Cape Colony
entries_new.mechanism: Griqua migrants settled land and set up their own government under one leader.
entries_new.story: Griqualand East, officially New Griqualand, was one of four short-lived Griqua states in southern Africa. It lay between the Umzimkulu and Kinira rivers, south of the Sotho kingdom, in land that had belonged to the Mpondo king Faku. Adam Kok III led the Griqua there after a long journey from the Cape and made Kokstad the capital. Britain occupied the territory and made it a colony in 1874, shortly before Kok died. It was soon incorporated into the neighbouring Cape Colony.
entries_new.anchor: Kokstad, KwaZulu-Natal and Eastern Cape border

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states
Wikipedia: Griqualand East

entries_new.name: Mahdist State
entries_new.story: The Mahdist State was a state in Sudan built on a religious and political movement that Muhammad Ahmad, later called the Mahdi, started in 1881 against the Khedivate of Egypt, which had ruled Sudan since 1821. Mahdist forces captured Khartoum and killed the British governor-general Charles Gordon. From 1885 the government claimed control of Sudanese territory from its capital Omdurman. Anglo-Egyptian forces ended it in 1898, though the list entry gives 1899.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states
Wikipedia: Mahdist State

entries_new.name: Dervish State
entries_new.mechanism: Armed resistance under a religious leader, with a council, fortified base and its own claim to rule the region.
entries_new.story: The Dervish State, also called the Dervish Movement, was an armed resistance movement and polity based at Taleh in northern Somalia from 1895 to 1920. Its leader, Mohammed Abdullah Hassan (Sayyid Mohamed), a poet and Sufi militant, called for independence from the British and Italian colonial powers and for the defeat of Ethiopian forces. A council of Sufi elders called the Khususi advised him. Wikipedia says about 25,000 young men joined between 1899 and 1905. British and Italian forces defeated the movement in 1920.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states
Wikipedia: Dervish State (Horn of Africa)

entries_new.name: Tripolitanian Republic
entries_new.stopped_by: Italy, helped by splits among the republic's leaders
entries_new.story: The Tripolitanian Republic was an Arab republic declared in western Libya after the First World War, in territory Italy had invaded and annexed in 1911. Its leaders took their case to the 1919 Paris Peace Conference and gained no backing from the Allied powers, and no state recognised it. It ended in the early 1920s after disputes among its leaders, rivalry between tribes and the lack of a single armed force. Italy reasserted control. The list gives its capital as Aziziya.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states
Wikipedia: Tripolitanian Republic

entries_new.name: South Kasai
entries_new.mechanism: Provincial leaders used the collapse of central authority at independence to set up an ethnic-based state.
entries_new.story: South Kasai was a state in the Kasai region of the newly independent Congo that was semi-independent from 1960 to 1962. Albert Kalonji, leader of a faction of the nationalist movement, built it around the Baluba people during the Congo Crisis, as violence spread and Katanga also broke away. It declared secession on 9 August 1960 and called on Baluba living elsewhere in the Congo to return. Wikipedia notes it never explicitly rejected Congolese sovereignty, and that its government called itself an autonomous part of a federal Congo. It was reintegrated in 1962.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states
Wikipedia: South Kasai

entries_new.name: Rwenzururu Kingdom
entries_new.stopped_by: Settlement making it an autonomous kingdom within Uganda
entries_new.mechanism: Declared independence from the Tooro Kingdom and held out against Uganda until a settlement.
entries_new.story: Rwenzururu is a region in western Uganda along the Rwenzori Mountains, home to the Konjo and Amba peoples. These peoples were placed under the Tooro Kingdom and wanted their own monarchy, which the colonial government denied. Isaya Mukirania, the first omusinga (king), declared independence from Tooro on 30 June 1962, about three months before Uganda's independence. About two decades of conflict followed and the kingdom ended as an autonomous kingdom inside Uganda. The Ugandan government officially recognised it on 17 March 2008.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states
Wikipedia: Rwenzururu

entries_new.name: Republic of Benin (1967)
entries_new.founder: Biafra, with Albert Nwazu Okonkwo as head of government
entries_new.mechanism: Biafran forces set up a client government in occupied territory.
entries_new.story: The Republic of Benin existed for about seven hours on 19 September 1967 during the Nigerian Civil War. Biafra, the breakaway state in south-eastern Nigeria, had occupied Nigeria's Mid-Western Region and created this puppet state around Benin City, with Albert Nwazu Okonkwo as head of government. Biafra hoped to stop non-Igbo residents of the region from siding with Nigeria. The declaration came as federal forces were retaking the region, and they entered Benin City the next day. Wikipedia reports the occupation turned residents against the secessionists and gave the Nigerian government grounds to escalate the war.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states
Wikipedia: Republic of Benin (1967)

entries_new.name: South Sudan Provisional Government and Nile Provisional Government
entries_new.stopped_by: Internal coup and the 1972 Addis Ababa Agreement
entries_new.story: During the First Sudanese Civil War, mostly Anyanya fighters formed the South Sudan Provisional Government in 1967 to seek separation of southern Sudan from the government in Khartoum, which was dominated by Arabic-speaking Muslims. Wikipedia describes it as divided by political wrangling and ethnic tension. It collapsed in 1969 and was reformed as the Nile Provisional Government, based at Juba, which tried to rename the project the Nile Republic. That body fell after a coup within about a year. Most separatists then accepted the 1972 Addis Ababa Agreement.
entries_new.anchor: Juba, southern Sudan (list gives Juba as the Nile government's capital)

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Maakhir State of Somalia
entries_new.story: Maakhir was a short-lived quasi-state in the Sanaag region of north-eastern Somalia, set up in 2007 and ended in 2009. The name is linked to the Warsangali clan and to a Warsangali sultanate that governed the coast for centuries. The list says it was proclaimed independent of both Puntland and Somaliland, whose territories it lay between, and was soon absorbed into Puntland. Its capital was Badhan. Wikipedia adds that a consultative conference on the region's self-determination was held in Badhan from 23 February to 11 March 2025, which elected representatives for an interim administration.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states
Wikipedia: Maakhir

entries_new.name: Democratic Republic of Bakassi
entries_new.story: The Bakassi Movement for Self-Determination (BAMOSD) declared a Democratic Republic of Bakassi in two stages. The decision came at a meeting in Yenagoa, Nigeria, on 2 July 2006, and independence was declared on 2 August 2006 after the Greentree Agreement under which Nigeria handed the disputed Bakassi peninsula to Cameroon. A second declaration followed on 31 July 2008 naming Akwa Obutong as capital. By 2009 Cameroon held full control of Bakassi, according to the list. Wikipedia says Nigerian and Cameroonian media have suggested outside backing for the movement.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states
Wikipedia: Bakassi Movement for Self-Determination

entries_new.name: Mohéli secession, 1997
entries_new.mechanism: Island leaders declared separation from the Comoros following Anjouan's lead.
entries_new.story: Mohéli, or Mwali, is the smallest of the main Comoro Islands. Migrants from Madagascar led by Ramanetaka took it from the Anjouan sultanate in 1830, France made it a protectorate in 1886, and it agreed to join the Comoros in 1975. Political, economic and social turmoil followed. On 11 August 1997, a week after Anjouan, Mohéli seceded, with Said Mohamed Soefu as president and Soidri Ahmed as prime minister. The island rejoined the Comoros in 1998.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states
Wikipedia: Mohéli

entries_new.name: Jubaland (1998 breakaway)
entries_new.story: Jubaland is the Juba Valley region of southern Somalia on the Kenyan border. In 1998, during the Somali Civil War, General Mohammed Said Hersi Morgan, a former defence minister and son-in-law of the late dictator Siad Barre, declared the region independent, with Bu'ale as capital. Allied Somali Forces ousted Morgan the next year. The region's administration then allied with the Transitional Federal Government in 2001, according to the list entry.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states
Wikipedia: Jubaland

entries_new.name: Republic of Azania (2011)
entries_new.mechanism: Politicians proclaimed a state abroad with a neighbouring government's backing.
entries_new.story: A group of Somali politicians proclaimed the Republic of Azania in Nairobi on 3 April 2011, with Mohamed Abdi Mohamed Gandhi as president. It claimed Jubaland in southern Somalia, most of which the armed group al-Shabaab then held. Kenya supported it as a buffer state and sent troops into Jubaland in October 2011. Somalia condemned the project, and other Jubaland players contested its legitimacy. Wikipedia says Azania had little real control and disappeared when delegates formed a new Jubaland government on 15 May 2013.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states
Wikipedia: Azania (Somalia)

entries_new.name: Free Province of Guayaquil
entries_new.stopped_by: Annexation to Gran Colombia by Simón Bolívar
entries_new.story: On 9 October 1820 revolutionaries in the port city of Guayaquil, in what is now Ecuador, overthrew Spanish rule in the October 9 Revolution. Under José Joaquín de Olmedo they declared a provisional government over the liberated areas. In July 1822 Simón Bolívar led a coup, named himself 'Supreme Leader' and annexed the province to Gran Colombia. The list entry says he saw Guayaquil as the gateway to liberating Peru.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: State of Los Altos
entries_new.story: Los Altos was a state of the United Provinces of Central America, centred on Quetzaltenango in western Guatemala. According to the Wikipedia list, Guatemala's ruling class was alarmed by Rafael Carrera, a peasant governor, and led six western provinces into secession under Liberal leadership. The new state asked the federation for recognition. In January 1840 Carrera reconquered Los Altos and in March defeated the federal army, which the list calls the death knell of the United Provinces. Los Altos rebelled again in 1847 when Carrera declared Guatemala an independent republic, and was quickly crushed.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Chan Santa Cruz
entries_new.founder: Maya rebels of the Caste War
entries_new.story: Chan Santa Cruz was a Maya territory in the south-east of what is now the Mexican state of Quintana Roo. Local Maya revolted in 1847 after the Republic of Yucatán's second secession from Mexico, driving nearly all white people from the Yucatán peninsula in the Caste War. After defeat, some rebels founded a stratified religious community in the jungle, the list says, which stayed a base for the rebel Cruzob for the next fifty years. After decades of campaigns by both sides, the Cruzob recognised the Mexican government in 1915.
entries_new.anchor: Felipe Carrillo Puerto (former Chan Santa Cruz), Quintana Roo

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Puerto Rico (Lares, 1868)
entries_new.story: On 23 September 1868 rebels in the town of Lares declared a Republic of Puerto Rico, in the Lares uprising against Spanish rule. Spain had repeatedly refused the island autonomy. The rebels were defeated by November at the latest, though the revolt brought limited political reforms. The list adds that anti-Spanish rebels declared independence again on 13 August 1898, near the end of the Puerto Rican campaign of the Spanish-American War, and also could not secure it.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Provisional Government of Assiniboia
entries_new.stopped_by: Negotiated entry as the province of Manitoba
entries_new.story: The Métis of the Red River settlement, led by Louis Riel, formed a provisional government during the Red River Rebellion of 1869 and 1870. They acted after Canada bought Rupert's Land from the Hudson's Bay Company and they feared direct rule from Canada. The list says they demanded self-government rather than outright independence. The government negotiated the region's entry into the Confederation of Canada as the province of Manitoba.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Provisional Government of Saskatchewan (1885)
entries_new.story: During the North-West Rebellion of 1885, Métis leader Louis Riel, who had led the Red River Rebellion in 1869, set up a self-declared Métis government at Batoche in what is now Saskatchewan. The Canadian army defeated it after just over two months of fighting. Riel was later found guilty of high treason and hanged.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Jungle Nation (Loreto)
entries_new.stopped_by: Vizcarra's death in a revolt at Moyobamba
entries_new.story: The Jungle Nation was the second attempt to form an independent state in the Department of Loreto in the Peruvian Amazon. Colonel Emilio Vizcarra, a soldier appointed prefect (regional governor) of the department, grew disillusioned with the national government and named himself 'Supreme Leader'. The list says the project ended when Vizcarra died on a tour of Loretan cities: in Moyobamba he was caught in a revolt and a thrown rock killed him. The first attempt was the 1896 Loretan Insurrection.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Federal State of Loreto (1896)
entries_new.story: The Loretan Insurrection of 1896 produced a Federal State of Loreto, proclaimed in Iquitos in the Peruvian Amazon by insurgents who wanted Peru to become a federal system. It sought autonomy within Peru rather than independence, according to the list. Many inhabitants did not support it, and a Peruvian expedition soon put it down.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: McDonald Territory
entries_new.challenge: State of Missouri and the US Congress
entries_new.story: In 1961 a provisional government in McDonald County, Missouri, chose the name McDonald Territory and tried to secede the county from Missouri. Missouri and the US Congress never recognised it. The Neosho Daily News called it a publicity stunt, and the list notes that people not involved rarely took its claim to independence seriously. It lasted about a year.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Airrecú
entries_new.story: Costa Rica had granted land rights to settlers along the San Juan River, which forms part of the border with Nicaragua. A dispute ended with Costa Rica acknowledging that the land belonged to Nicaragua and promising to remove the settlers. The settlers refused and in June 1993 declared independence as the Republic of Airrecú, a name the list says means 'friendship' in a local Indian language. The Nicaraguan Army moved in and escorted the Republic into Costa Rica.
entries_new.anchor: San Juan River border area, Nicaragua and Costa Rica

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Provisional Revolutionary Government of Cibao
entries_new.story: On 7 July 1857 a civic and military movement began in Santiago de los Caballeros, in the Cibao valley of the Dominican Republic, to overthrow conservative president Buenaventura Báez. The Cibaeños declared themselves governed by a provisional revolutionary government seated in Santiago. The list dates this government from 1857 to 1861.
entries_new.anchor: Santiago de los Caballeros, Dominican Republic

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: State of Buenos Aires
entries_new.story: On 11 September 1852 the province of Buenos Aires overthrew the Argentine Confederation's government within its borders and set itself up as a separate State of Buenos Aires. It stayed apart for nine years. It rejoined the Argentine Confederation after its victory at the Battle of Pavón in 1861, according to the list.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Manipur State (1947 to 1949)
entries_new.stopped_by: Manipur Merger Agreement, accession to India
entries_new.challenge: Diplomatic pressure on the King, per the list
entries_new.story: Manipur was a princely state of the British Indian Empire from 1891 to 1947. It was granted independence at midnight on 14 August 1947. From then until October 1949 the region was de jure independent, meaning independent in law. King Bodhchandra Singh then acceded to India on 15 October 1949 under the Manipur Merger Agreement, which the list says followed intense diplomatic pressure.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: State of Pasundan
entries_new.stopped_by: Incorporation into the Republic of Indonesia
entries_new.recognition: Backed by the Dutch colonial government
entries_new.story: Pasundan was a Dutch-backed state in West Java. Musa Suriakartalegawa established the Pasundan Republic on 4 May 1947 with the support of the Dutch colonial government, and it became the State of Pasundan on 26 February 1948 with Bandung as capital. It was incorporated into the newly independent Republic of Indonesia on 27 December 1949 and dissolved on 11 March 1950. The Indonesian province of West Java succeeded it.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Free Dadra and Nagar Haveli
entries_new.story: Dadra and Nagar Haveli were two exclaves of the Portuguese district of Daman in western India. In 1954 supporters of integration with the Indian Union invaded and occupied them, and the territory then enjoyed de facto independence until India formally annexed it in 1961. Portugal continued to treat it as Portuguese territory until 1974, and native citizens could obtain Portuguese citizenship until 2006, according to the list.
entries_new.anchor: Silvassa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, India

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Timor (1961)
entries_new.story: After the failed Viqueque rebellion of 1959 in Portuguese Timor, a group called the Battle Office for the Liberation of Timor formed in early 1961 under Maoclao, with backing from Indonesia, according to the list. A republic was proclaimed at the border town of Batugade on 9 April 1961. Portuguese troops quickly put it down. The list names a short-lived successor, the Democratic Republic of East Timor, recognised by seven states.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Azadistan
entries_new.story: Azadistan was a short-lived state in Iranian Azerbaijan that lasted from early 1920 until September that year, with its centre in Tabriz. Mohammad Khiabani, a member of the Iranian parliament who opposed both Soviet influence and British colonialism, founded it. He and his followers chose the name Azadistan to protest the use of the name 'Azerbaijan' for the Baku-based republic in the Caucasus. They also meant it as a model of freedom for the rest of Iran.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Alash Autonomy
entries_new.stopped_by: Bolshevik ban on the Alash party
entries_new.story: The Alash Autonomy was a provisional Kazakh government in Central Asia, based at Semey. Kazakh elites founded it in 1917, when the area was part of the Russian Republic and then Soviet Russia. Its ruling Alash party aimed for autonomy within Russia and a national, democratic state. The Bolsheviks banned the party and the autonomy was disestablished in 1920. It bordered Russian territory to the north and west, the Turkestan Autonomy to the south and China to the east.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Great Mongol State (Bogd Khanate)
entries_new.challenge: Qing dynasty, then Republic of China
entries_new.story: In 1911 the 8th Bogd Gegeen of Outer Mongolia proclaimed independence from China's Qing dynasty. After 1915 it was a de facto self-governing autonomous region under the suzerainty of the Republic of China. After a rebellion against Chinese rule in 1919 to 1921 it reaffirmed independence and became the predecessor of the Mongolian People's Republic. The list notes that internationally the territories it held were widely regarded as part of the Republic of China.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Tuvan People's Republic
entries_new.challenge: Republic of China, then the Soviet Union
entries_new.recognition: Soviet Union and the Mongolian People's Republic
entries_new.story: The Tuvan People's Republic was an attempt by Tuvans to gain independence after centuries of Chinese rule and years of domination by Imperial Russia. It had its capital at Kyzyl. The Soviet Union put it under Soviet control and later formally annexed it. The list says only the Soviet Union and the Mongolian People's Republic recognised its independence, and that internationally the territory it held was widely recognised as part of the Republic of China.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Negros
entries_new.stopped_by: Annexation by the United States into the Philippine Islands, 1901
entries_new.story: The Republic of Negros was a government on the island of Negros in the Philippines at the end of Spanish rule, with its capital in Bacolod. The list says it existed under a local constitution in cooperation with the US military government from 2 October 1899. On 20 April 1901 the province of Occidental Negros was established and the United States annexed it to the Philippine Islands, still under the name Republic of Negros.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Revolutionary Government of the Republic of Indonesia (PRRI)
entries_new.story: The Revolutionary Government of the Republic of Indonesia was set up in Sumatra in 1958 to oppose the central government of Indonesia, with Padang as its base. It is often grouped with the Permesta rebellion, but the list stresses that Permesta was a separate movement in Sulawesi, which pledged allegiance to the PRRI on 17 February 1958. The list gives 1961 as the end of the revolutionary government.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Revolutionary Serbia
entries_new.recognition: Ottoman Empire, as an autonomous region in 1807 (rejected by the revolutionaries)
entries_new.story: Revolutionary Serbia was the state Serbian revolutionaries created in Ottoman Serbia (the Sanjak of Smederevo) after the First Serbian Uprising against the Ottoman Empire began in 1804. Its capitals were Topola and Belgrade. The Ottoman government first recognised it as autonomous in January 1807, but the revolutionaries rejected that treaty and kept fighting the Ottomans until 1813.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Pontecorvo
entries_new.story: Pontecorvo was an exclave, a piece of territory cut off from the rest of its state, belonging to the Papal States. In April 1820 the Carbonari, a secret revolutionary society, declared it seceded from the Papal States. Pontecorvo twice asked to join the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies, and both requests were refused, because that kingdom would only deal with the exclave's affairs through the Pope. Austrian forces occupied it in March 1821 and restored it to the Papal States.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Italian United Provinces
entries_new.story: The Italian United Provinces were a short-lived republic set up in 1831 across some Papal States territories (Romagna, Marche and Umbria) and the Duchies of Parma and Modena. It began on 5 February, after a popular uprising in Bologna declared the temporal power of the Pope and the Emilian dukes revoked. It ended on 26 April, the day Austrian troops took the city of Ancona.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of San Marco
entries_new.story: After the unrest of 1848 the Republic of San Marco was proclaimed in Venetia with Venice as capital, and it allied with other Italian states against the Austrian Empire. It voted to federate under the Kingdom of Sardinia, then returned to independence after the Piedmontese defeat. Only Venice and its lagoon stayed under its control. It surrendered after almost five months of siege, having existed for 17 months.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Gurian Republic
entries_new.story: The Gurian Republic, or Gurian peasant republic, was an insurrection in the western Georgian province of Guria, then part of the Russian Empire, before and during the Russian Revolution of 1905. The republic itself existed from November 1905 to 10 January 1906, according to the list. Its seat was Ozurgeti.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Central Albania
entries_new.story: The Republic of Central Albania was declared after Ottoman forces withdrew from the former Albanian Vilayet (province). Essad Pasha Toptani declared it, with Durrës as capital. It ended in 1914 when the troops of William of Wied, the prince installed as ruler of Albania, took control of the country. The list names Albania as the country now covering its territory.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Vorarlberg
entries_new.stopped_by: Blocked by the Allies and Austria
entries_new.challenge: The Allied powers and the Austrian government
entries_new.story: As Austria-Hungary collapsed, the people of Vorarlberg proclaimed themselves a separate, non-Austrian Germanic people and declared the Republic of Vorarlberg on 3 November 1918, with Bregenz as capital. The Allies and the new Austrian republican government blocked the secession. In April 1919 over 80 percent of Vorarlbergers voted to leave Austria and join Switzerland, and that was blocked too, according to the list.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Lajtabánság (Leitha Banate)
entries_new.story: Lajtabánság was a state declared in 1921 in the Burgenland region of Austria by ethnic Hungarians, after the Treaty of Trianon forced Hungary to give up the territory. Oberwart was its capital. It ceased to exist after about a month, when Austria annexed it, according to the list, which names Austria and Hungary as the countries concerned.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Zakopane
entries_new.story: The Republic of Zakopane was an area in Galicia centred on Zakopane that formed its own parliament, the 'National Organisation', on 13 October 1918. Its main goal was to join an independent Polish state. On 30 October it declared independence from Austria-Hungary and two days later renamed itself the 'National Council'. The Polish Liquidation Committee took control of Galicia and disestablished it on 16 November.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Banat Republic
entries_new.stopped_by: Serbian invasion and partition of the Banat, 1919
entries_new.story: The Banat Republic was set up in the Banat region, now partly in Serbia, by members of the region's ethnic groups, and it had its capital at Timișoara. Only Hungary recognised it. Serbia invaded, and in 1919 the Banat was partitioned between Hungary, Romania and the newly created Yugoslavia. The list gives Romania, Serbia and Hungary as the countries now covering the former area.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Mirdita
entries_new.story: The Republic of Mirdita was set up by Albanian Catholics who wanted to break away from Albania, a mainly Muslim country. The list gives Prizren as its capital and Albania as the country now covering its territory. Yugoslavia backed it, but it lasted only three months, and the list gives no start date.
entries_new.anchor: Mirdita, northern Albania (list gives Prizren as capital)

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Mountainous Armenia
entries_new.story: The Republic of Mountainous Armenia was an anti-Soviet Armenian state that existed from 26 April to 13 July 1921, with Goris as capital. It roughly matched what are now the Armenian provinces of Vayots Dzor and Syunik, plus parts of present-day Azerbaijan. The list names Armenia and Azerbaijan as the countries now covering its territory.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of North Ingria
entries_new.stopped_by: Peace Treaty of Tartu, reintegration into Russia
entries_new.story: North Ingria was a state of Ingrian Finns in the southern Karelian Isthmus. It seceded from Bolshevik Russia after the October Revolution and aimed to be incorporated into Finland. Established on 23 January 1919, it ruled parts of Ingria until 5 December 1920. The Peace Treaty of Tartu returned the area to Russia.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Uhtua (East Karelia)
entries_new.story: The Republic of Uhtua, also called the Republic of East Karelia, was an unrecognised Finnish-led state that existed from 1919 to 1920. It was created from five volosts (rural districts) of the Kemsky uyezd in the Arkhangelsk Governorate, an area now in the Republic of Karelia. Its capital was the village of Uhtua, now Kalevala.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Carpatho-Ukraine
entries_new.mechanism: An autonomous region declared independence as Czechoslovakia was dissolved.
entries_new.story: Carpatho-Ukraine was an autonomous region within the Second Czechoslovak Republic, created in December 1938 and renamed from Subcarpathian Rus', whose autonomy a constitutional law of 22 November 1938 had confirmed. The First Vienna Award of 2 November 1938 had already returned the mostly Hungarian-populated south to Hungary. After Czechoslovakia broke up, the region proclaimed itself an independent republic on 15 March 1939, headed by President Avgustyn Voloshyn. Nazi Germany sided with Hungary, and Hungary and Poland invaded, crushing local resistance by 18 March 1939.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Carpatho-Ukraine
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Ossola Partisan Republic
entries_new.challenge: Italian Social Republic and German forces
entries_new.story: The Ossola Republic was a partisan republic in northern Italy set up on 10 September 1944 and recaptured by Fascist forces on 23 October 1944. In a little over a month it built an organised administration, including the Provisional Government Council of Domodossola for the liberated zone. The period is remembered in Italy as the Forty Days of Freedom.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Perloja
entries_new.story: After the First World War, people in Perloja in southern Lithuania set up a self-governing parish committee, often called the Republic of Perloja. The list says it had its own court, police, prison and currency, the Perloja litas, and an army of 300 men. It is dated 1918 to 1923, and the village lies in what is now Lithuania.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Central Lithuania
entries_new.story: The Republic of Central Lithuania was a short-lived puppet state of Poland, with Vilnius as capital, that no other state recognised. It was founded on 12 October 1920, after Żeligowski's Mutiny, in which soldiers of the Polish Army, mainly the 1st Lithuanian-Belarusian Infantry Division under Lucjan Żeligowski, attacked Lithuania with the support of the Polish air force, cavalry and artillery. Poland incorporated it on 18 April 1922.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Kholodny Yar Republic
entries_new.story: The Kholodny Yar Republic was a self-proclaimed state and partisan movement in the Chyhyryn district of the Kyiv province, now Cherkasy Oblast, in the Kholodny Yar forest. It covered part of the lands of the former Ukrainian People's Republic, and the village of Melnyky was its capital. Its army of about 15,000 men was made up of peasants and soldiers of the Ukrainian People's Republic's army, which the White Army had earlier defeated in Podolia.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Hutsul Republic
entries_new.stopped_by: Invasion by the Hungarian Soviet Republic, then absorption into Czechoslovakia
entries_new.story: The Hutsul Republic was a state formed in the Carpathian territory of the former Lands of the Crown of Saint Stephen, with Yasinia as capital. It originally intended to join the West Ukrainian People's Republic. The Hungarian Soviet Republic invaded it in June 1919, and it then became part of the First Czechoslovak Republic.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Irish Republic (1919 to 1922)
entries_new.stopped_by: Anglo-Irish Treaty and the Irish Free State
entries_new.story: The Irish Republic was an unrecognised Irish nationalist state during the Irish War of Independence, with Dublin as its capital. It ceased to exist after the Anglo-Irish Treaty, which gave Southern Ireland independence as the Irish Free State while Northern Ireland stayed under British control. The list says these terms led much of the victorious Irish Republican Army to reject the treaty, producing the Irish Civil War of 1922 to 1923 between pro-treaty Free State forces and the Anti-Treaty IRA, who viewed the dissolution of the Republic as illegal.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Kingdom of Norway (1814)
entries_new.stopped_by: Convention of Moss: personal union with Sweden
entries_new.story: After the Treaty of Kiel at the end of the Napoleonic Wars gave Norway to Sweden, Norway refused the treaty and declared its independence in 1814. It adopted a constitution and elected the Danish Prince Christian Frederik as king, with Oslo as capital. A short war with Sweden followed, and Norway accepted a personal union with Sweden, meaning the two countries shared a king, in the Convention of Moss.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Partisan republics of Alto Monferrato, Bobbio and Carnia
entries_new.story: In 1944 Italian resistance fighters held several districts for short periods and ran them as partisan republics. The Republic of Alto Monferrato existed from September to 2 December 1944, after two resistance movements based in Nizza Monferrato and Costigliole d'Asti united. The Republic of Bobbio centred on Bobbio in Piacenza province and ran about 90 kilometres from the Val Trebbia to the Oltrepò Pavese. The Republic of Carnia was a short-lived state around Ampezzo.
entries_new.anchor: Nizza Monferrato, Bobbio and Ampezzo, northern Italy

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: North Caucasian Emirate
entries_new.story: The North Caucasian Emirate was a mainly Avar and Chechen Islamic state in Chechnya and western Dagestan from September 1919 to March 1920, during the Russian Civil War. Its temporary capital was the village of Vedeno. Its leader, Uzun Hajji Saltinsky, held the title Imam and Emir of the North Caucasus.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Bashkurdistan
entries_new.stopped_by: Annexation by the Russian SFSR, March 1919
entries_new.story: After the Russian Revolution the All-Bashkir Qoroltay, a national convention, decided that an independent Bashkir republic was needed. On 15 November 1917 the Bashkir Regional Council, led by Äxmätzäki Wälidi Tıwğan, proclaimed it in areas with a mostly Bashkir population in the Orenburg, Perm, Samara and Ufa provinces. The list calls it the first democratic Turkic republic in history. The Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic annexed it in March 1919, and the Bashkir Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic succeeded it.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Autonomous Palatinate
entries_new.stopped_by: Bavarian anti-separatist group (Viking League), per the list
entries_new.story: The Autonomous Palatinate was a separatist state in the Palatinate region of Germany, with Speyer as its seat. Franz Josef Heinz founded it in 1924, at about the same time as separatist activity in the Rhineland. The list says the Bavarian anti-separatist group known as the Viking League brought it down, assassinating Heinz and carrying out several massacres against his supporters.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Slovak People's Republic (1918)
entries_new.story: The Slovak People's Republic was a short-lived state at Košice that lasted from 11 to 29 December 1918. The Eastern Slovak National Council, set up in November 1918 alongside the Slovak National Council, led it. Viktor Dvorčák, an advocate and former archivist from Prešov who worked for the Hungarian revisionist movement, led the council.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: United Tribes of New Zealand
entries_new.founder: James Busby and northern Māori chiefs
entries_new.story: In 1835 the British Resident James Busby and northern Māori chiefs declared the independence of the United Tribes of New Zealand, with Waitangi as its centre. According to the list, the declaration was meant to safeguard British claims against French territorial expansion. It led to the Treaty of Waitangi, a formal treaty between Māori leaders and the British Crown, in 1840.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Kingdom of Fiji (Cakobau)
entries_new.story: Ratu Seru Cakobau, paramount chief of the island of Bau, declared himself King of Fiji, and other chiefs saw him at best as first among equals. In June 1871 the British honorary consul John Bates Thurston persuaded the chiefs to accept a constitutional monarchy with Cakobau as king, but with real power in a cabinet and legislature dominated by Australian settlers. The Legislative Assembly first met at Levuka in November 1871. Government overspending led to unmanageable debt, and in 1872 Thurston approached Britain, at Cakobau's request, with an offer to cede the islands. The list dates Cakobau's kingdom from 1852.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Fiji
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Kingdom of Easter Island (Dutrou-Bornier)
entries_new.story: Jean-Baptiste Dutrou-Bornier, a French sailor, bought up much of Easter Island after its population had severely declined, and declared his Indigenous wife its queen. The list calls the result the Kingdom of Easter Island, with Anakena as capital. The kingdom ended after Dutrou-Bornier's death, when the island's population had fallen to 111 people.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Kingdom of Rapa Nui (independence claims after 1888)
entries_new.story: After Chile annexed Easter Island (Rapa Nui) in 1888, the islanders believed, because of a misunderstanding in the treaty, that they kept their sovereignty. King Riro Kāinga tried to negotiate the island's continued sovereignty with Chile and died in what the list calls mysterious circumstances. Several other islanders then declared themselves kings, including Enrique Ika, Moisés Tuʻu Hereveri and María Angata. The list dates the movement from 1888 to 1914.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Kingdom of Bora Bora
entries_new.stopped_by: French vice-resident replaced the last queen, 1895
entries_new.recognition: France and the United Kingdom, 1847 (Jarnac Convention)
entries_new.story: The Kingdom of Bora Bora formed in the early 19th century when the island was unified, and France and the United Kingdom recognised it in 1847 through the Jarnac Convention. It also took in Tupai, Maupiti, Maupihaa, Motu One and Manuae, and was one of several independent Polynesian states in the Society Islands. France formally annexed it in 1888, but the list says Bora Bora stayed officially neutral during the fighting in the Leeward Islands, and the French could not take control until 1895, when the last queen, Teriimaevarua III, was replaced by a French vice-resident.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Bora Bora
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Kingdom of Raiatea-Tahaa resistance government
entries_new.founder: Queen Tuarii (installed by the resisting chiefs)
entries_new.story: Raiatea and Tahaa were a Polynesian kingdom in the Leeward Islands that resisted French annexation. King Tamatoa VI of Raiatea asked for a French protectorate, but many lesser chiefs refused to accept French authority and deposed him. They set up a resistance government and installed Queen Tuarii on the throne. The list dates this from 1888 to 1897, with Uturoa as capital.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Independent Commune of Franceville
entries_new.recognition: Independence guaranteed by France, per the list
entries_new.story: From 1878 the New Hebrides (now Vanuatu) were neutral territory under an Anglo-French naval commission that claimed no jurisdiction over internal native affairs. Colonists wanted a working government, and on 9 August 1889 Franceville, on Efate, declared itself an independent commune under an elected mayor-president, Ferdinand-Albert Chevillard. It practised universal suffrage without distinction of sex or race, though only white men could hold office, among about 500 islanders and fewer than 50 white residents. It was soon suppressed, and by June 1890 was reported to be practically broken up. The list says France guaranteed its independence.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Franceville, New Hebrides
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: State of Quito
aka: First Cry of Hispanic American Independence
entries_new.founder: Juan Pío Montúfar (president of the first Junta)
entries_new.stopped_by: Royalist troops from Lima and New Granada
entries_new.mechanism: Local elites formed a ruling Junta in the Spanish colonial capital after King Ferdinand VII's abdication in 1808.
entries_new.story: On 10 August 1809 a group of local intellectuals and Criollos (American-born Spanish colonists) in Quito deposed the Spanish president of the Real Audiencia and formed a provisional Junta under Juan Pío Montúfar. The Junta still recognised King Ferdinand VII but not the local Spanish authorities. Royalist troops from Lima and New Granada defeated its 2,000-man army, and members were arrested on 24 October 1809. A second Junta ran from September 1810 to October 1811. Ecuador marks 10 August as its national day.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Quito Revolution (1809 to 1812)
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Cabanagem (Grão-Pará)
entries_new.pop: About 100,000 in the province; 30 to 40 percent estimated to have died
entries_new.story: The Cabanagem was a popular revolution and separatist movement in the province of Grão-Pará in the Empire of Brazil from 1835 to 1840. Its causes included extreme poverty among the Paraense people, oppression by the Empire, and the political irrelevance of the province after Brazil's independence. The name comes from the huts of the poorest people along the waterways, mostly caboclos, freed slaves and Indigenous people. Wikipedia reports that 30 to 40 percent of the province's estimated 100,000 people died. The list names Belém as its capital.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Cabanagem
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of the Rio Grande
aka: Provisional Government of the Northern Frontier
entries_new.founder: Antonio Canales Rosillo and Jesús de Cárdenas
entries_new.mechanism: Federalist leaders withdrew recognition from the central government and set up a provisional government, aiming to restore a federal system.
entries_new.story: The name Republic of the Rio Grande was given by the Anglo-American press and later historians to a federalist revolt and provisional government in northeastern Mexico between 1838 and 1840. On 23 January 1840 a junta at Casa Blanca on the Nueces River, led by Antonio Canales Rosillo, Jesús de Cárdenas and others, withdrew recognition from the centralist government in Mexico City and installed the Provisional Government of the Northern Frontier. Wikipedia notes the leaders' own documents do not use the word republic or speak of independence. The revolt ended with the agreement signed at Camargo on 6 November 1840.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Republic of the Rio Grande
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Yucatán (1841 to 1848)
entries_new.stopped_by: Rejoined Mexico in exchange for military aid
entries_new.laws: Constitution of 1841 (individual rights, religious freedom, amparo)
entries_new.challenge: Mexico, and the Caste War uprising
entries_new.mechanism: The peninsula declared independence from a centralising Mexican government and rejoined for military help.
entries_new.story: The second Republic of Yucatán began in 1841 when Yucatán declared independence from the Centralist Republic of Mexico, and it stayed independent for seven years. Its Constitution of 1841 guaranteed individual rights, religious freedom and a new legal form called amparo, a court order protecting a person's rights. The area covered the modern Mexican states of Yucatán, Campeche and Quintana Roo. The Caste War of 1847 led Yucatán to ask Mexico for military aid, which Mexico gave on condition that Yucatán rejoin the Mexican Federation. A first republic in 1823 had joined the federation within seven months.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Republic of Yucatán
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Independent State of Acre
entries_new.founder: Luis Gálvez; later José Plácido de Castro
entries_new.cost: Bolivia received two million pounds sterling, land in Mato Grosso and a railway
entries_new.mechanism: Brazilian settlers and an expedition declared a republic in Bolivian territory, aiming to join Brazil.
entries_new.story: Acre was a rubber-producing region assigned to Bolivia in 1867 but settled mostly by Brazilians. A Spanish journalist, Luis Gálvez, led a 1899 to 1900 expedition secretly financed by the Amazonas state government and declared a First Republic of Acre on 14 July 1899. Brazil's government sent troops to arrest him in March 1900, and a Second Republic was also suppressed. José Plácido de Castro, leading an army that reached 30,000 men, proclaimed a Third Republic on 27 January 1903. The Treaty of Petrópolis of 11 November 1903 had Bolivia cede Acre to Brazil in exchange for land in Mato Grosso, two million pounds sterling and a railway.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Republic of Acre
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Celestial Monarchy (Contestado)
entries_new.challenge: Landowners, state police and the Brazilian military
entries_new.mechanism: A religious leader proclaimed a monarchy among settlers in a disputed border region.
entries_new.story: The Contestado War was a guerrilla war for land in southern Brazil between October 1912 and August 1916, between settlers and landowners backed by state police and the military. The region was called Contestado because Paraná, Santa Catarina and Argentina all claimed it. A messianic state, the Celestial Monarchy, was declared at Taquaruçu by José Maria de Santo Agostinho amid anger among local farmers and workers over land confiscation and railroad construction. The war was marked by the religious faith of the rebellious caboclos, who saw themselves as in a religious war.
entries_new.anchor: Taquaruçu, Contestado region, Santa Catarina, Brazil

entries_new.name: Rupununi uprising
entries_new.mechanism: Ranchers and Amerindian communities rose to separate a region from Guyana, allegedly with Venezuelan support.
entries_new.story: The Rupununi uprising was a secessionist insurrection in southwest Guyana that began on 2 January 1969, less than two years after independence. Cattle ranchers led it and sought control of 22,300 square miles (58,000 square kilometres) of land. The Guyana Defence Force dispersed the rebels, and their leaders fled to Venezuela. Several academic sources, as cited by Wikipedia, say Venezuela supported and equipped the rebels, at a time when Venezuela was pressing a historic claim to the land west of the Essequibo River.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Rupununi uprising
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Confederation of the Equator
entries_new.challenge: Empire of Brazil under Pedro I
entries_new.mechanism: Provincial liberals rebelled against the new empire's centralised constitution.
entries_new.story: The Confederation of the Equator was a short-lived secessionist rebellion in northeastern Brazil in 1824, fought in the provinces of Pernambuco, Ceará and Paraíba. Liberals led it in opposition to the authoritarian, centralising policies of Emperor Pedro, Brazil's first ruler. Its main leaders in Pernambuco, Manuel de Carvalho Pais de Andrade and Friar Joaquim do Amor Divino Rabelo e Caneca, were republicans who had taken part in the 1817 revolt and been pardoned. They had accepted the monarchy hoping for provincial autonomy, and the highly centralised Constitution of 1824, issued after Pedro dissolved the Constituent Assembly in 1823, frustrated that hope.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Confederation of the Equator
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Pernambucan Revolution (1817)
entries_new.mechanism: Revolutionaries in the captaincy tried to set up an independent government.
entries_new.story: The Pernambucan revolution, also called the Priest's Revolution or Seventeen, took place in the Captaincy of Pernambuco in northeastern Brazil. Wikipedia says the decline of sugar production and the influence of Freemasonry sparked it, together with the struggles for independence in Spanish colonies, the independence of the United States and liberal ideas. Domingos José Martins led it, with support from Antônio Carlos Ribeiro de Andrada and Frei Caneca, and the US consulate in Recife publicly backed the revolutionaries. It is notable as one of the first attempts to set up an independent government in Brazil.

entries_new.name: First Philippine Republic (Malolos Republic)
entries_new.stopped_by: Capture of Aguinaldo by US forces, 1901
entries_new.recognition: None; remained a de facto government
entries_new.mechanism: A revolutionary government wrote a constitution and fought US forces after Spain ceded the islands.
entries_new.story: The First Philippine Republic, also called the Malolos Republic, was established in Malolos, Bulacan, by the Malolos Constitution of 23 January 1899, succeeding the Revolutionary Government of the Philippines. Emilio Aguinaldo was its first president. No foreign power recognised it, though it remained a de facto government. The Revolutionary Government considered the 1898 Treaty of Paris, which passed Spain's claim to the United States, invalid. Fighting with American forces began on 4 February 1899. Aguinaldo was captured on 23 March 1901 and declared allegiance to the US on 19 April 1901, effectively ending the Republic.

sources.t: Wikipedia: First Philippine Republic
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Biak-na-Bato
entries_new.mechanism: Revolutionary leaders declared a republic in a mountain base, then agreed a ceasefire and left the country.
entries_new.story: The Republic of Biak-na-Bato was a Filipino revolutionary government declared by Emilio Aguinaldo in 1897 during the Philippine Revolution against Spain, based at San Miguel. In 1897 Aguinaldo's forces also signed a ceasefire with the Spanish authorities, and he and other leaders went into exile in Hong Kong. Wikipedia notes that this government, like one earlier at Tejeros, styled itself the Republic of the Philippines, but its founding documents were not drafted by an elected congress as the later Malolos Constitution was.

sources.t: Wikipedia: First Philippine Republic
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Kingdom of Kurdistan (Sulaymaniyah)
entries_new.stopped_by: British forces, including an Assyrian force and the RAF
entries_new.story: The Kingdom of Kurdistan was a short-lived, self-proclaimed Kurdish state declared in Sulaymaniyah after the collapse of the Ottoman Empire, in territory under the British Mandate of Mesopotamia. Sheikh Mahmud Barzanji, head of a Sufi order, had already declared an independent Kurdistan in May 1919 and been defeated in June. On 10 October 1921 a statement in Sulaymaniyah established a Kurdish government with Barzanji as king. Wikipedia dates the kingdom September 1921 to July 1925, but also says British-led forces took Sulaymaniyah in July 1924, and the list gives 1921 to 1924.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Kurdistan
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Fujian People's Government
aka: People's Revolutionary Government of the Republic of China
entries_new.founder: Li Jishen (chairman) with Cai Tingkai, Chen Mingshu and Jiang Guangnai
entries_new.mechanism: Army commanders broke with the national government and proclaimed a rival republic in their province.
entries_new.story: The Fujian People's Government was a short-lived anti-Kuomintang government that set up a socialist republic in China's Fujian Province from 22 November 1933 to 13 January 1934. Leaders of the 19th Route Army, including Cai Tingkai, Chen Mingshu and Jiang Guangnai, had been sent to suppress a Communist rebellion and instead negotiated peace with it. They broke with Chiang Kai-shek, took control of Fujian and proclaimed the new government with Li Jishen as chairman. It first had popular support, but high taxes and fear of a new civil war during Japanese aggression eroded it, and Nationalist forces crushed it.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Fujian People's Government
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: United Suvadive Republic
entries_new.recognition: Supported briefly by Britain, per the list
entries_new.story: The United Suvadive Republic was a breakaway state from the Sultanate of Maldives made up of three southern atolls: Addu, Huvadhu and Fuvahmulah. Abdulla Afeef Didi was its first president. Wikipedia says the southern atolls had been richer than the north through farming and direct trade, and had long governed themselves through hereditary family leaders. The list dates it 1959 to 1963 and says Britain supported it briefly before abandoning it, while the article dates the republic from 1958.

sources.t: Wikipedia: United Suvadive Republic
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Persian Socialist Soviet Republic (Gilan)
entries_new.challenge: Persian central government and British forces
entries_new.mechanism: A partisan movement proclaimed a republic with Red Army assistance after British forces withdrew from the Caspian coast.
entries_new.story: The Persian Socialist Soviet Republic, also called the Gilan Republic, was a short-lived unrecognised Soviet republic in north-west Persia, south of the Caspian Sea, with its capital at Rasht. It lasted from June 1920 to September 1921. Mirza Kuchik Khan, leader of the Constitutionalist Movement of Gilan, and his Jangali partisans founded it with help from the Soviet Red Army. In May 1920 a Soviet fleet had entered the port of Anzali, saying it was pursuing Russian vessels taken there by the White general Denikin, and the British garrison left without resistance.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Persian Socialist Soviet Republic
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Democratic Republic of Yemen (1994)
entries_new.stopped_by: Forces of the Republic of Yemen, July 1994
entries_new.story: On 21 May 1994 Ali Salem al-Beidh declared on Aden Radio the creation of the Democratic Republic of Yemen as an independent state with Aden as its capital, during the 1994 Yemeni Civil War. He called it the nucleus of a unified Yemen. The Summer War between it and the Republic of Yemen ran from May to 7 July 1994 and killed between 1,000 and 7,000 people. The Republic of Yemen government won and describes the war as a defence of unity. The list says the breakaway state lasted six weeks before being reconquered.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Democratic Republic of Yemen
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Brunei revolt and the Kalimantan Utara republic
entries_new.story: The Brunei revolt of 1962 was an insurrection in the British protectorate of Brunei by opponents of the monarchy's proposed inclusion in the Federation of Malaysia. The insurgents belonged to the TNKU (North Kalimantan National Army), a militia supplied by Indonesia and linked to the Brunei People's Party, which favoured a pro-Indonesian North Borneo Federation. They attacked the oil town of Seria, police stations and government buildings, but the revolt began to break down within hours. It failed to capture Brunei Town or the Sultan, and it influenced the Sultan's decision in 1963 not to join Malaysia. The list calls it a failed attempt to set up a republic.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Brunei revolt
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Islamic Emirate of Kurdistan
entries_new.mechanism: An Islamist party controlling one governorate declared independence.
entries_new.story: The Islamic Emirate of Kurdistan was an unrecognised Kurdish state in the Halabja Governorate of Iraq, set up after the Gulf War. It had been outside Iraqi government control since 1991 and was a self-governing entity within the Kurdistan Region in 1994, when the Kurdistan Islamic Movement was given Halabja Governorate in a three-way division of control that followed the KDP-PUK civil war. It officially declared independence in 2001 and dissolved after Operation Viking Hammer in 2003.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Islamic Emirate of Kurdistan
Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Local republics of the 1905 Russian Revolution
entries_new.story: During the 1905 revolution in the Russian Empire, workers, soldiers and peasants in many places declared local self-governments they called republics. The list names Lyubotyn (26 to 30 December 1905), Shuliavka in Kyiv (12 to 16 December, old style), Chita (November 1905 to January 1906), Krasnoyarsk (9 to 27 December), Novorossiysk (12 to 26 December), Ostrowiec (from 27 December to mid-January 1906), Zagłębie and Sławków (about 10 to 12 days each) and Markovo, a peasant state of six villages that lasted from 18 October 1905 to 18 July 1906.
entries_new.anchor: Markovo, Volokolamsk district, Russia (one of many local republics)

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Provisional governments of the Greek Revolution
entries_new.story: During the Greek War of Independence against the Ottoman Empire, several regional provisional governments governed liberated areas, which the list calls unrecognised protostates. They include the Messenian Senate at Kalamata (1821), the Achaean Directory at Patras (1821 to 1822), the Peloponnesian Senate at Tripoli, the Senate of Western Continental Greece at Missolonghi (1821 to 1823), the Areopagus of Eastern Continental Greece at Amfissa (1821 to 1825), the military-political system of Samos (1821 to 1834) and a provisional government on Crete (1822). The First Hellenic Republic at Nafplio (1822 to 1832) was known as the Provisional Administration of Greece until 1827.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Republic of Rotuma
entries_new.story: Shortly after the September 1987 coup in Fiji, a Rotuman man named Henry Gibson told newspapers that the island of Rotuma was independent. He cited human rights violations by the military-backed regime and the lack of Rotuman representation in Fijian politics. A small group of soldiers arrested Gibson and his fellow protesters, and the separatists were charged with sedition.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Tibet (de facto independence, 1912 to 1951)
entries_new.story: In 1913 the 13th Dalai Lama proclaimed Tibet's independence from China's Qing dynasty, a declaration recognised only by Mongolia, which was itself unrecognised. The list says there were doubts about the authority of the Tibetan representative who signed that treaty. In 1914 a treaty accepting Chinese suzerainty was signed and the border was adjusted in favour of British India. The 14th Dalai Lama acknowledged Chinese sovereignty in the Seventeen Point Agreement of 1951. China rejects the 1914 treaty and claims South Tibet, now part of India's Arunachal Pradesh. Internationally, the territory was widely regarded as part of China.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Tatarstan's sovereignty declaration (1990 to 2002)
entries_new.stopped_by: 2002 constitution defining Tatarstan as part of Russia
entries_new.story: On 30 August 1990 the Tatar Soviet Socialist Republic declared its sovereignty, with Kazan as capital. In 1992 Tatarstan held a referendum on a new constitution, which about 62 percent of those who voted approved. The 1992 constitution defined Tatarstan as a sovereign state. The Russian Constitutional Court declared the referendum and the constitution unconstitutional. The constitution as introduced in 2002 defines Tatarstan as part of the Russian Federation and removes the term 'sovereignty'.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Free State of Jones
entries_new.story: Jones County, Mississippi, lay in a state that had seceded from the United States and joined the Confederacy. Inhabitants who were loyal to the Union set up a government of their own, the Free State of Jones, with Laurel as its seat. A small militia raised by the inhabitants made it nearly impossible for the Confederacy to collect taxes there. The list says the Free State ended after the defeat of the Confederates.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of historical unrecognized states

entries_new.name: Confederated Republic of Altai
entries_new.story: The Confederated Republic of Altai was an attempt to set up an independent Altai during the Russian Civil War, with Gorno-Altaysk as capital. The list says its long-term aim was to merge with neighbouring Tuva and Khakassia to restore the 17th-century Dzungar Khanate, with Turkic leadership. It is dated 1918 to 1922.

entries_new.name: Provisional Government of Western Thrace
entries_new.stopped_by: Treaty of Constantinople and Ottoman withdrawal
entries_new.mechanism: Local leaders declared an autonomous state with Ottoman military support to avoid Bulgarian rule.
entries_new.story: This short-lived unrecognised republic covered about 8,600 square kilometres of Western Thrace between the Maritsa and Mesta rivers, from 31 August to 25 October 1913, with Gümülcine (now Komotini) as capital. Bulgaria had been awarded the area, but after the Second Balkan War local Muslims and Greeks refused Bulgarian control and an autonomous state was declared with Ottoman support. Under British pressure, Bulgaria and the Ottomans signed the Treaty of Constantinople, and the Ottomans withdrew. Wikipedia also reports atrocities against Bulgarian civilians by Ottoman irregular forces during this period.

entries_new.name: Free Cities of Menton and Roquebrune
entries_new.stopped_by: Became protectorates of the Kingdom of Sardinia, May 1849
entries_new.mechanism: Two towns left their principality over taxation and declared themselves free cities.
entries_new.story: Menton and Roquebrune seceded from the Principality of Monaco in May 1848, during the Revolutions of 1848, and joined as the Free Cities. Monaco had been a protectorate of the Kingdom of Sardinia since the Congress of Vienna, which Wikipedia says left its economy stagnant. Monegasque authorities raised taxes, and the two towns carried much of that load. After a brief period of autonomy the cities became protectorates of the Kingdom of Sardinia in May 1849.

entries_new.name: Sonderbund
entries_new.challenge: Swiss Federal Diet and federal army
entries_new.mechanism: Seven cantons formed a separate alliance and prepared to defend it by arms against the confederacy.
entries_new.story: In 1845 seven mainly Catholic Swiss cantons (Lucerne, Fribourg, Valais, Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden and Zug) formed the Sonderbund, meaning 'separate alliance', to protect their interests against a centralisation of power in the loose Swiss confederacy. The Federal Diet declared it unconstitutional in October 1847 and ordered it dissolved by force. General Guillaume Henri Dufour led a federal army of 100,000 and defeated the Sonderbund forces in a campaign from 3 to 29 November 1847 that cost about 100 lives. Switzerland then became a federal state.

entries_new.name: West Ukrainian People's Republic
entries_new.story: The West Ukrainian People's Republic was a short-lived state that controlled most of Eastern Galicia from November 1918 to July 1919. It emerged during the break-up of Austria-Hungary and claimed Lviv, Ternopil, Kolomyia, Drohobych, Boryslav, Stanyslaviv and part of Peremyshl, along with northern Bukovina and Carpathian Ruthenia. In January 1919 it nominally united with the Ukrainian People's Republic as its Western Oblast. Poland also claimed the territory and by July occupied most of it, and the government went to the Ukrainian People's Republic, according to the list.

entries_new.name: Republic of Heinzenland
entries_new.mechanism: Local Social Democrats proclaimed a republic in a town on the Austria-Hungary language frontier.
entries_new.story: The Republic of Heinzenland, nicknamed the Two-Day Republic, was a short-lived, unrecognised state in what is now the Austrian state of Burgenland. It aimed to protect the German-speaking population of western Hungary during disputes over whether the area would go to Austria or Hungary after the First World War. On 5 December 1918 (some sources say 6 December) the Social Democratic politician Hans Suchard, with local workers and Social Democrats in Mattersburg, proclaimed it. Wikipedia says this was done without sufficient knowledge of the balance of power in the area.
